resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register spells it Villas Lookout; the statewide list and OpenStreetMap say Vilas. The coordinates and registry number match (US 1226, WI 30), so this is one tower. The story keeps the Register's spelling.
The Register gives 1,703 ft (519 m); OpenStreetMap gives 506 m for the node. The story uses the Register's figure and notes the gap.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. NHLR is the only detailed source, and it gives design, administrator, the October 1936 build, and the August 2017 registration. The statewide list confirms standing. No staffing, fire, access or rental information was found. Unresolved lead, not used: a Wisconsin Historical Society Facebook post, readable only as a search snippet, describes a 1932 Aeromotor tower moved by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1935 with a cabin built in 1936; the snippet does not name Villas, so it is not used and should not be assumed to be this tower. Current ownership after the state's 2015 decision is unknown; NHLR still lists the DNR, which may be out of date, and the Register does not say whether Villas was one of the 72 towers. Access is unknown. The brief's record matches NHLR; no corrections. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the NHLR coordinates (N 45.236839, W 089.307953) and the OpenStreetMap node (45.2368463, -89.3079481) agree, so the 506 m node is the same point; the 13 m elevation gap is unexplained, and the story says so. The story's 2015 wording now dates the decommissioning (WJFW) rather than a Wisconsin decision, since the Door County Pulse article is undated. No photos added.
